D009-D011_h001.question:
It kind of feels like I live in two different gears, and neither one is really working for me.

For most of this past year, it’s like a cloud settled over everything. I used to be proud of clearing cases, but lately, even when we close a tough one, I just feel… nothing. My wife will say she’s proud, my lieutenant will compliment me, and I just nod. Inside, it’s like, “So what?” Getting through paperwork or even reading a report wears me out mentally in minutes; my brain feels like it’s slogging through mud. I’ve gotten so low at times that I actually sat in my car outside the pharmacy, thinking about buying a bunch of pills and just ending it. I’ve even stashed a bottle at home “just in case.”

But then, about a month ago, it flipped. I’ve been wound up, snapping at people over tiny things—a typo in a report, someone chewing too loud. I can’t sit still in briefings; I’m pacing the back of the room, drumming my fingers. I’m talking nonstop—my partner jokes he can’t get a word in—and I’ve got this restless energy, like I need to be moving, doing something. I barely sleep, maybe a couple hours, and I don’t even feel tired.

There’s this constant edge of nervousness under it all—like I’m always bracing for something—but I can’t tell if that’s from the job, from my mood, or both. My work has definitely taken a hit during the low parts; I’ve been slower, missing small details, and my supervisor’s noticed. At home, my wife says she doesn’t know which version of me she’s coming home to anymore.
D009-D011_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D009-D011_h001.answer: D & A. Bipolar II Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D009-D011_h002.question:
I don’t really know how to explain it… For about a year now I’ve mostly felt like I’m moving through mud. I wake up tired, go to bed tired, even on days when I don’t work or I sleep in. Things that used to feel good, like getting complimented on a job or finishing a big pour on site, just feel… whatever. My boss says I do solid work, but it doesn’t mean much to me anymore.

A few months back, though, there was this stretch, maybe a month, where I was the opposite. I was on edge and snapping at guys over small stuff—someone misplacing a tool and I’d blow up. I couldn’t sit still on breaks; I’d walk around the site, looking for extra tasks, volunteering to stay late, trying to take on more jobs than usual. I barely slept for several nights at a time but didn’t feel like I needed it, just kept going.

During that time I talked a lot, like I couldn’t let there be silence, even after work with the guys or at the bar. Underneath all of this, I worry a lot—about money, getting injured, ending up alone—but I’m not sure if that’s just normal stress.

The low periods get so heavy that a few months ago I actually gathered up a bunch of painkillers and thought about taking them all at once. I didn’t go through with it, but I scared myself. It’s been hard to keep working regularly since then.
D009-D011_h002.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D009-D011_h002.answer: D & A. Bipolar II Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D009-D011_h003.question:

Then, about a month ago, it flipped. I suddenly had this rush of energy. I barely slept for several nights and didn’t really care—I’d just keep working, pacing, jumping from idea to idea. I couldn’t sit still. I was calling old contacts, setting up coffees, talking nonstop in meetings, way more outgoing than I usually am. D009-D011_h004.question:

D009-D011_h006.question:

But I was still paying my bills, cooking, going to appointments.

Then it sort of “dropped off,” and for the last two months I’ve felt flat, like my feelings are wrapped in cotton. I wake up at 4 a.m. most days and just lie there, blank, unable to fall back asleep. I’ve been neglecting chores, skipping social activities, struggling to manage the house alone. Underneath it all is this constant, uneasy worry—about my health, my memory, money—though I can’t tell if the worrying is causing all this or just going along with it.

A. Specific Phobia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D009-D011_h006.answer: C & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D009-D011_h007.question:

Then it kind of flipped. For the last two months I’ve been really down and exhausted. I cry easily, sometimes for no clear reason—like if I get a bad grade or after a fight with my mom, I just lose it. I sleep a ton: long nights, then naps after school, and I still feel drained. I’ve fallen behind in classes and barely have energy to hang out. I do feel on edge a lot, sort of tense and worried, but I’m not sure if that’s causing everything or just part of it.
D009-D011_h007.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D009-D011_h007.answer: C & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D009-D011_h008.question:

D009-D011_h009.question:
